options.value: Upper Elementary / Tweens (9-12 years) – Fluent Readers

options.value: Pre-Teens & Early Teens (12-14 years) – Confident Readers
options.desc: Rich storytelling, intricate character arcs, themes of identity, coming-of-age, leadership, responsibility, and occasional darker themes (loss, self-discovery, ethics)

Pre-Readers - Simple words and short phrases, Repetitive, rhythmic, or rhyming text, Focus on everyday objects, animals, and basic concepts (e.g., colors, numbers, emotions)

Emerging Readers - Short and simple sentences, Introduction to storytelling (beginning, middle, end), Basic problem-solving themes, Simple moral lessons (sharing, kindness, emotions), Interactive elements (repetition, call-and-response, counting)

Early Readers - Short paragraphs, basic punctuation, Simple dialogue, Slightly more complex storylines with basic conflicts, Introduction to humor, adventure, or fantasy, Moral lessons with relatable scenarios

Developing Readers - Longer sentences with more descriptive language, Introduction to more complex emotions and problem-solving, Independent reading ability starts to develop, Stronger character development and relationships, Light humor, adventure, and fantasy themes

Fluent Readers - More advanced vocabulary and longer sentences, Complex conflicts and moral dilemmas, Deeper character development, Themes can include friendship, teamwork, courage, and overcoming obstacles, Light sci-fi, historical fiction, and mythology elements

Confident Readers - Full-fledged storytelling with deeper themes, More intricate character arcs and relationships, Themes may include identity, coming-of-age, leadership, and responsibility, Some darker themes (e.g., loss, self-discovery, ethical dilemmas)

Advanced Readers - Advanced vocabulary and intricate storytelling, Themes of love, rebellion, personal growth, and self-reflection, Strong world-building (for fantasy, sci-fi, or dystopian stories), May include moral ambiguity and nuanced conflicts
